entries.content_plain: CHAPTER 62 Is 62:1-12 . Intercessory Prayers for Zion's Restoration, Accompanying God's Promises of It, as the Appointed Means of Accomplishing It. 1. I-- the prophet, as representative of all the praying people of God who love and intercede for Zion (compare Is 62:6 , 7 ; Psa 102:13-17 ), or else Messiah (compare Is 62:6 ). So Messiah is represented as unfainting in His efforts for His people ( Is 42:4 ; 50:7 ). righteousness thereof-- not its own inherently, but imputed to it, for its restoration to God's favor: hence "salvation" answers to it in the parallelism. "Judah" is to be "saved" through "the Lord our (Judah's and the Church's) righteousness" ( Jr 23:6 ). as brightness-- properly the bright shining of the rising sun ( Is 60:19 ; 4:5 ; 2Sa 23:4 ; Pr 4:18 ). lamp-- blazing torch.

(<reference osisRef="Zech.9.16">Zec 9:16</reference>)<div eID="gen16529" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16530" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">in ... hand of ... Lord--</hi>As a crown is worn on the head, not "in the hand," hand must here be figurative for "under the Lord's protection" (compare <reference osisRef="Deut.33.3">De 33:3</reference>). "All His saints are in thy hand." His people are in His hand at the same time that they are "a crown of glory" to Him (<reference osisRef="Rev.6.2">Re 6:2</reference>; <reference osisRef="Rev.19.12">19:12</reference>); reciprocally, He is "a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty" to them (<reference osisRef="Isa.28.5">Is 28:5</reference>; compare Mal 3:17). <div eID="gen16530" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 3. ( Zec 9:16 ) in ... hand of ... Lord-- As a crown is worn on the head, not "in the hand," hand must here be figurative for "under the Lord's protection" (compare De 33:3 ). "All His saints are in thy hand." His people are in His hand at the same time that they are "a crown of glory" to Him ( Re 6:2 ; 19:12 ); reciprocally, He is "a crown of glory and a diadem of beauty" to them ( Is 28:5 ; compare Mal 3:17).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv9490"/><div sID="gen16546" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv9490"/>10. What Isaiah in the person of Messiah had engaged in (<reference osisRef="Isa.62.1">Is 62:1</reference>) unrestingly to seek, and what the watchmen were unrestingly to pray for (<reference osisRef="Isa.62.7">Is 62:7</reference>), and what Jehovah solemnly promised (<reference osisRef="Isa.62.8">Is 62:8</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.62.9">9</reference>), is now to be fulfilled; the Gentile nations are commanded to "go through the gates" (either of their own cities [Rosenmuller] or of Jerusalem [Maurer]), in order to remove all obstacles out of "the way of the people (Israel)" (see on <reference osisRef="Isa.7.14">Is 7:14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.40.3">Is 40:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.52.10-Isa.52.12">52:10-12</reference>).<div eID="gen16546" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen16547" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">standard--</hi>for the dispersed Jews to rally round, with a view to their return (<reference osisRef="Isa.49.22">Is 49:22</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.11.12">11:12</reference>). <div eID="gen16547" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 10. What Isaiah in the person of Messiah had engaged in ( Is 62:1 ) unrestingly to seek, and what the watchmen were unrestingly to pray for ( Is 62:7 ), and what Jehovah solemnly promised ( Is 62:8 , 9 ), is now to be fulfilled; the Gentile nations are commanded to "go through the gates" (either of their own cities [Rosenmuller] or of Jerusalem [Maurer]), in order to remove all obstacles out of "the way of the people (Israel)" (see on Is 7:14 ; Is 40:3 ; 52:10-12 ). standard-- for the dispersed Jews to rally round, with a view to their return ( Is 49:22 ; 11:12 ).
